title: The probe census and the flake-harness result it ingests
$comment: The four ROOT definitions are `census_v1`, `census_v2`, `census_v3` and `flake_result_v1`; tools/probe_census.py maps each declared schema string to one of them. They are deliberately not named after the schema strings themselves, because a JSON Pointer treats `/` as a separator and `#/$defs/probe-census/v2` would name nothing.
description: The declared shape of every document tools/probe_census.py reads or writes (#1492). It replaces hand-rolled type, presence, closed-object, enum, length and range checking; it deliberately declares NO cross-field invariant -- those span fields, so no keyword expresses them and they live in tools/probe_census.py's census_invariants()/result_invariants() (#1493) -- and no parity with the live probe registry, which stays validate_manifest's report and --seed's repair. Every object here is closed: explicit `required` plus `additionalProperties: false`, with a nullable field REQUIRED and null-inclusive rather than optional, so deleting one is a violation rather than an absence. Enums are spelled as one-element `enum` rather than `const` on purpose: the library's const message names only the value it EXPECTED, while enum names the offending one.

census_v1.$comment: #1425's seed: the inventory alone, with no census record. Declared so --seed can validate what it migrates FROM, and so a stored v1 census is reported as schema drift rather than as corruption.

census_v2.$comment: #1428's record: the same inventory, each row carrying its census. FROZEN at the six-field record, because this is now a migration INPUT: it must keep describing what a stored v2 census actually looks like, so `--seed` can validate the document it migrates from. Pointing it at the current `inventory_row` would make every real v2 census invalid for carrying no `claims`, which is the one thing migration exists to add.

census_v3.$comment: #1434's record: the v2 document with each row's census also carrying its append-only `claims` log. Claim acquisitions are a DEDICATED collection rather than more `attempts`, which tools/probe_census.py defines as result-ingestion attempts and deliberately makes non-idempotent.

inventory_row_v2.$comment: A stored v2 row. Frozen alongside census_v2 and never widened.

census_record_v2.$comment: A stored v2 record: the six fields #1428 wrote, with no `claims`. Frozen -- it describes migration INPUT, so widening it would make every real v2 census invalid.

acceptable_failures.$comment: X (#1430): the failures a complete 10-run measurement may show and still be acceptable, so 0 through 9 -- an X of 10 would declare a probe that never passes acceptable. Still null-INCLUSIVE here, and only here: a census written before the policy existed holds nulls, and tools/probe_census.py's --seed has to be able to read one in order to initialize it to 0. policy_invariants() is what refuses a null on every candidate and on --validate.

estimated_worst_case_seconds.$comment: Supplied metadata, distinct from a sample's OBSERVED worst_elapsed_seconds.

current.$comment: The current commit cohort, or null when nothing has been measured. Spelled as if/else rather than oneOf so a malformed cohort reports the field that is actually wrong instead of `is not valid under any of the given schemas`.

census_record.$comment: Exactly the seven fields probe_census.empty_census() writes.

acceptable_failures.$comment: X (#1430): the failures a complete 10-run measurement may show and still be acceptable, so 0 through 9 -- an X of 10 would declare a probe that never passes acceptable. Still null-INCLUSIVE here, and only here: a census written before the policy existed holds nulls, and tools/probe_census.py's --seed has to be able to read one in order to initialize it to 0. policy_invariants() is what refuses a null on every candidate and on --validate.

estimated_worst_case_seconds.$comment: Supplied metadata, distinct from a sample's OBSERVED worst_elapsed_seconds.

current.$comment: The current commit cohort, or null when nothing has been measured. Spelled as if/else rather than oneOf so a malformed cohort reports the field that is actually wrong instead of `is not valid under any of the given schemas`.

claims.$comment: #1434's append-only log of successful claim ACQUISITIONS, keyed for idempotency by `token`. Deliberately not `attempts`, which are result-ingestion attempts and are non-idempotent by design.

claim.$comment: Exactly what probe_claim.Claim.census_record() writes: one successful acquisition of the per-probe lock, recorded BEFORE the measurement it authorizes runs. `token` is the acquisition token and the idempotency key -- replaying the same acquisition must remain one record, and the same token carrying different metadata is refused rather than appended.

pid.$comment: NOT `count`: a pid is not a tally and legitimately exceeds that definition's million -- Linux allows a pid_max up to 2^22.

cohort.$comment: One commit's accumulated samples. Append-only; the writer never rewrites one.

sample.$comment: Exactly what probe_census.summarize_sample() keeps: summarized outcomes and artifact REFERENCES. Every producer-only field is absent by closure, not by an exclusion list.

sample_run.$comment: One run as the census keeps it: the producer's `port` and per-run `checks` map are dropped.

attempt.$comment: Exactly what probe_census.summarize_attempt() keeps: one well-formed ingestion attempt, accepted or not.

flake_result_v1.$comment: The INGESTION document, exactly as probe_flake.Measurement.to_document() writes it. Declared here rather than in tools/probe_flake.py, which is out of scope for #1492: this is the consumer's intake contract.

error_run.$comment: The one run whose protocol stream could not be trusted, or null. Never a member of `runs`, and never a fourth probe outcome. if/else for the same reason as `current`.

checks.$comment: The probe's own check descriptor: ordered id/label pairs.

result_run.$comment: One valid run of the harness. `checks` is the per-run check map; declaring it an OBJECT is what refuses the truthy non-dict that used to raise AttributeError.

harness_error_run.$comment: Structurally a run, but carrying the one outcome `runs` may never hold.

run_checks.$comment: check id -> that run's result for it.

check_counts.$comment: check id -> its PASS/FAIL/MISSING tally across the measurement.

protocol_status.$comment: probe_flake.protocol_status()'s two answers today. A future probe-result version is a deliberate edit here, not something to leave open.

run_outcome.$comment: The three outcomes a VALID run may report. HARNESS_ERROR is not one: it labels error_run alone.

commit_sha.$comment: A 40-hex commit, or the literal `unknown` probe_flake records when git could not be consulted.

capabilities.$comment: RTS capabilities and peak concurrency. Positive is what the producer guarantees: probe_flake refuses --rts-caps below 1 and --runs below 1, and the concurrency registry floors its own count at 1.
